openai.feedback:
- Category: spec  
  Severity: high  
  File: `shared/scripts/tools/stamp_test_results.py:118-148`  
  Finding: The stamping tool is implemented but is not wired into the test-results producer. The specification explicitly requires adding the invocation after the prompt-written record is produced in `plugins/shipwright-test/agents/test-runner.md`; no test-plugin/agent file is changed in this diff. Consequently, normal test runs will continue to produce unstamped records, failing AC2 despite the existence of a usable standalone tool.  
  Suggestion: Add the post-write invocation in the test runner’s record-writing flow, passing only a code-resolved run context or allowing the tool to resolve it itself, and ensure a tool failure makes the phase visibly fail rather than silently leaving an unstamped record.

- Category: spec  
  Severity: medium  
  File: `shared/scripts/tools/stamp_test_results.py:129-132`  
  Finding: The test-record `run_id` is accepted directly from `--run-id` when it is syntactically valid. This permits a prompt/caller to provide an arbitrary but valid wrong run ID, contrary to the requirement that every stamp value be resolved by code rather than supplied by prompt instruction. The config fallback does not fix this because the CLI value takes precedence.  
  Suggestion: Resolve the run ID from the authoritative run configuration/event data inside the tool, or validate an optional CLI-provided ID against that authoritative value and reject mismatches.

- Category: bug  
  Severity: medium  
  File: `shared/scripts/source_state.py:~116-126` (`safe_run_id`) and `shared/scripts/source_state.py:~153-181` (`parse_banner_line`)  
  Finding: `safe_run_id` accepts internal spaces, while the banner format and parser treat the run ID as a whitespace-delimited token (`run=(\S+)`). For example, `SourceState(run_id="run one")` renders as `Source-State: run=run one`, but parses back as `run_id="run"`. A run ID such as `x clean` or `x commit=deadbeef` can also cause the parser to report a false clean state or forged commit token. This violates AC6’s markdown round-trip requirement and undermines provenance integrity.  
  Suggestion: Reject all whitespace in run IDs so they are actually single tokens, or define an escaping/encoding scheme and parse that scheme symmetrically. Tests should cover spaces and banner-reserved substrings such as `clean` and `commit=`.

- Category: security  
  Severity: low  
  File: `shared/scripts/source_state.py:~116-126` (`safe_run_id`)  
  Finding: The control-character check covers only ASCII C0 and DEL. It permits Unicode C1 controls (for example U+0085) and Unicode line separators such as U+2028, which can be treated as line breaks by downstream renderers or text processors. The specification requires rejecting a run ID containing a newline or control character so an untrusted event cannot forge banner content.  
  Suggestion: Reject Unicode control and line-separator characters, e.g. use Unicode categories (`Cc`, and line/paragraph separators) or reject non-printable characters; if the format remains token-based, reject all whitespace as well.

- Category: spec  
  Severity: low  
  File: `plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/audit_staleness.py:53-57`  
  Finding: The `Source-State:` banner matching/strip shape is duplicated in `audit_staleness.py` even though `shared/scripts/source_state.py` defines `BANNER_STRIP_RE` and `strip_banner()` specifically for this serialization. This conflicts with AC1’s requirement that one module own the markdown banner form. Divergence between these regexes could make renderer/parser behavior differ from staleness normalization.  
  Suggestion: Import and use `strip_banner()` (or `BANNER_STRIP_RE`) from `source_state.py`, with the same path-bootstrap approach used by the compliance provenance adapter.

- Category: test  
  Severity: medium  
  File: `shared/scripts/source_state.py:1-298`; `shared/scripts/tools/stamp_test_results.py:1-149`  
  Finding: No tests are included for the new serialization and I/O boundary. In particular, there is no evidence covering AC6/AC8/AC9: JSON and markdown round-trips including unresolved state, repeated stamping replacement semantics, corrupt-record no-write behavior, git failure/empty-repository handling, artifact exclusion from dirty detection, or all five compliance renderers having exactly one adjacent `Source-State:` line. The whitespace parsing defect above would pass without such tests.  
  Suggestion: Add focused unit tests for `source_state`, integration tests for `stamp_test_results.py` using temporary git repositories, and renderer/staleness tests verifying the five-document banner placement and normalization behavior.

Overall assessment: **block**. The core test-results producer is not actually wired to invoke the new tool, so the primary artifact it is meant to stamp will remain unstamped in normal operation; the banner format also currently fails round-trip integrity for accepted run IDs.
